/-!
# Primes and perfect squares

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landau%27s_problems#Near-square_primes)
-/


namespace PrimesAndPerfectSquares

/--
Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p - 1$ is a perfect square? In other words: Are there infinitely many primes of the form $n^2 + 1$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem infinite_prime_sq_add_one :
    answer(sorry) ↔ {n : ℕ | Prime (n^2 + 1)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end PrimesAndPerfectSquares

reformulations.difference: Lean asks whether infinitely many natural-number inputs n make n²+1 prime; the source counts distinct primes p=n²+1 for integer n, equivalently primes p with p−1 a perfect square.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On ℕ, Prime is equivalent to Nat.Prime. The map n ↦ n²+1 is injective, and its image on the qualifying inputs is exactly {p : ℕ | Nat.Prime p ∧ IsSquare (p−1)}. Integer roots give the same values as their natural absolute values. Since primes satisfy p≥2, natural subtraction introduces no discrepancy. Both infinitude equivalences, and the equivalence with an arbitrary Prop-valued answer slot, were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without sorry or reliance on the problem theorem.
